claims.claim: The case must pass a merits test to get legal aid.
claims.quote: An individual may qualify for legal representation only if the Director is satisfied that the following criteria are met
claims.note: The Civil Legal Aid (Merits Criteria) Regulations 2013 set general merits criteria that must be met for each form of civil legal aid.

claims.claim: The merits test considers the case's chances of success.
claims.quote: The prospects of success criterion is only met if the Director is satisfied that the prospects of success are—
claims.note: The prospects of success criterion applies to full (and investigative) representation, not to every form of legal aid such as legal help or family help.

claims.claim: The merits test considers whether the case is proportionate to its cost.
claims.quote: there is likely to be sufficient benefit to the individual, having regard to all the circumstances of the case, including the circumstances of the individual, to justify the cost of provision of legal help.
claims.note: The regulations require the benefit to the individual to justify the cost, and set cost benefit and proportionality tests for full representation.
